diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber's router has not checked in for 7.4 hours, exceeding the danger threshold. The EPON ONU, PON port, OLT, optical levels, VLAN, RADIUS state, and subscriber session are healthy, so the fault is isolated to router reachability or its management path rather than the fibre access network.
evidence: The trigger reports a router heartbeat age of 7.4 hours, which is in the danger range above the 4-hour threshold.
The ONU is online and responding, with live RX power of -20.61 dBm and TX power of 2.40 dBm, both normal.

Seven days of optical telemetry are stable: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX is near the 2.3 dBm mean, distance remains constant at 152, and TX bias remains healthy without a rising trend.
All tested ONUs on EPON0/2 are online, the OLT is reachable and healthy, and OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and PON checks are normal.
The customer VLAN is present and correctly mapped to VLAN 1062, and RADIUS records are present and consistent.
The subscriber has a current session with normal-duration history and only one session in the last 24 hours, so there is no evidence of session flapping or authentication failure.
The last router check-in and subscriber disconnect occur at the same time, while the ONU remains online, isolating the likely interruption to the router or its management/uplink path.
The evidence indicates a router-scoped incident, not a PON, OLT, fibre, RADIUS, or ONU fault.

remediation.action: Verify router reachability and management connectivity for TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01, including power, uplink, management interface, and routing/firewall access. Check router logs and uptime around 2026-09-19T20:01:00Z; restore or restart the router if it is unresponsive, then confirm heartbeat recovery and normal customer traffic. Do not replace the ONU, clean the fibre, or change the PON configuration unless router-side checks are normal and the heartbeat remains stale.

ground_truth.root_cause: The BNG TK_AZ_Bitola_Jadranska01 stopped checking in 7.4 hours ago. Customers behind it lost their sessions at the same moment. The optical plant is entirely unaffected: ONUs remain registered and are returning normal signal readings.
expected_reasoning: Router heartbeat is 7.4 hours stale, past the 4 hour danger threshold
The ONU is online with RX -20.6 and TX 2.4, both normal, and the live probe confirms it
Every peer on the port is also online with normal optical readings
OLT ping, SNMP and device metrics are all healthy
So the optical layer is working and the fault is not in the fibre plant
Sessions across customers on this router ended together 7.4 hours ago
Throughput fell to zero at the same moment while the ONUs stayed registered
Healthy ONUs with dead sessions is the router signature: the optical layer carries no traffic without the BNG
The blast radius follows the router, not the OLT, so every customer it serves is affected
distractors: ONU status is online everywhere, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The OLT health check reports healthy, which is correct but irrelevant
Optical readings are perfect, which points away from where the fault is
